findings.interval: binomial 95 % bound on a stated zero
findings.status: Measured. Readout correction demonstrated 17 Nov on kingston, fez and marrakesh (see Calibrations): on qubits stated at zero, correcting with the published figure leaves +0.12 to +0.20 points more misreads per readout than correcting with a same-job measurement. The same-job correction is built from separate calibration circuits and scored on held-out test circuits never used to build it, so the comparison is not circular (qubits stated at zero: kingston 10, fez 8, marrakesh 13). At the level of Bell-pair fidelity, Phase 2 found no difference between the two corrections on any chip.

findings.what: Published properties unchanged for days; a snapshot of an intermittent qubit held in place
findings.ibm: backend.properties(): readout entries normally refresh about daily, all 156 qubits together; fez q155 prob_meas1_prep0 = 0.982 (readout_error 0.497), not listed as faulty; target measure error on (155,) 0.497
findings.ours: Read 18 Nov 2026, about 12:00 UTC: ibm_phoenix's published properties are unchanged since 13 Nov UTC. ibm_fez, ibm_kingston, ibm_boston and ibm_pittsburgh published nothing new from 13 Nov until 18 Nov 08:46-09:46 UTC; their newest records carry 18 Nov stamps, but every readout entry is still the old one (fez 9 Nov, kingston and pittsburgh 12 Nov, boston 13 Nov) and most T1 entries likewise. ibm_marrakesh published again from 18 Nov 03:51 UTC (new initialization errors and a few gate entries first) and refreshed its readout and T1 entries at 18 Nov 08:21 UTC; ibm_chicago kept publishing (newest record 18 Nov 05:09 UTC), but only its readout entries are new (dated 18 Nov, except P(0|1) on 7 of 120 qubits still 10 Nov); its T1 and T2 entries date from 10 Nov. Fez's readout entries are dated 9 Nov 23:54 UTC. Fez q155 enters real bad-readout episodes lasting hours (15 of our 205 hourly calibration runs since 30 Oct, 7 %). IBM's last readout refresh before the record stopped, 9 Nov 23:54 UTC, caught the end of one: it states P(1|0) = 0.982; our hourly runs three and one hours earlier (20:54 and 22:54 UTC) had already read 0.936 and 0.995, and our next run, about one hour after the refresh (00:57 UTC), read 0.008. Since then the record has kept that snapshot. Under it, from our first run after IBM's refresh (10 Nov 00:57 UTC) to 18 Nov 03:52 UTC, 117 of our 129 hourly runs read P(1|0) 0.003-0.023, 3 read 0.03-0.11, and 9 were further episodes (0.21-0.86). Marrakesh q64 and q76 follow the same pattern (IBM's refresh at 13 Nov 03:47 UTC states 0.497 and 0.467; our hourly runs had read q64 at 0.21-0.44 from 23:24 UTC and q76 at 0.52-0.79 from 01:19 UTC, both still elevated 21 minutes after the refresh and back near their usual values within hours; good in about 95 % of hours since). Marrakesh's 18 Nov 08:21 UTC refresh replaced both: q64 P(1|0) 0.002, q76 0.096. Laid out from the published target, an 80-qubit GHZ circuit leaves q155 out (5 of 5 seeds); with q155's measure error set to its usual value it uses it (5 of 5). Avoiding a qubit with bad episodes is not clearly a harm, so this shows a layout change only.
findings.interval: 99 % Clopper-Pearson on 8,192 shots per prepared state (readout run, 17 Nov) and 12,500 (in-session calibration of the combination run, 18 Nov)
findings.math: record entry versus the same qubit measured hourly (prepare 0 and 1, 1,000 shots each, 99.9 % Clopper-Pearson) while that entry was in force; record versions compared entry by entry across our saved copies since 28 Oct
findings.repro_ibm: from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService; b = QiskitRuntimeService().backend('ibm_fez'); p = b.properties(); print(p.last_update_date, p.qubit_property(155)['prob_meas1_prep0'], b.target['measure'][(155,)].error)
findings.repro_ours: About 2 seconds of QPU on your own account: prepare |0> on qubit 155 and measure, 4,096 shots (QuantumCircuit(156, 1); qc.measure(155, 0); transpile with initial_layout=[155] is implied by the physical index), then count how often it reads 1 and compare with prob_meas1_prep0 above. Same for |1> (add qc.x(155) first) against prob_meas0_prep1. Our raw counts and scripts are available on request.
findings.status: Record fact (as read 18 Nov 2026, about 12:00 UTC) and hardware measurement

calibrations.name: Per-qubit phase correction after each readout (virtual Rz from a measured table)
calibrations.prior_art: Prior work includes Krinner et al., Nature 605, 669 (2022)
calibrations.result: 17 Nov 2026, fez, kingston, marrakesh (repeat of the 31 Oct run, predictions written and hashed before the data): a table measured minutes before gives back 0.90 [0.82, 0.92] (fez), 0.93 [0.88, 0.96] (kingston) and 0.86 [0.74, 0.91] (marrakesh) of the kick. The 27-day-old table still gives back 0.82 (fez) and 0.90 (kingston); on marrakesh the kick moved by +0.95 degrees since 21 Oct and the old table overshoots by +0.94, as predicted (prediction miss +0.01). 31 Oct 2026: kingston 0.92 (10-day table) and 0.93 (fresh); marrakesh 0.80 fresh. Null control: with the same data and the table scrambled across qubits, the correction gave back more than half the kick in 0 of 6,000 draws on kingston and marrakesh (exact 95 % upper bound 0.12 %), so the measured table, not any correction, does the work.
calibrations.cost: no QPU time to apply; about 11 s to measure a table
calibrations.status: Demonstrated on hardware, 31 Oct and 17 Nov 2026
calibrations.client: Entanglement quality lost on untouched qubit pairs over 8 readouts, without / with a table measured before the job (17 Nov 2026): kingston -14.8 / -0.4 points; fez -5.2 / -0.1; marrakesh -2.7 / +0.0 (99 % intervals in the source).

calibrations.name: Measure T1 and T2 before an idle-heavy job instead of trusting the published values
calibrations.client: Coherence an idling circuit keeps, published-T2 forecast / measured (17 Nov 2026): kingston q121 50 % / 28 %; marrakesh q91 67 % / 51 %; fez q148 78 % / 57 %. The published figure over-forecasts by 16 to 22 points on all three, including kingston q121 where the published pair looks physically valid. Sample: three qubits on one day, two of them chosen because their published pair breaks the physical bound; a chip-wide rate needs randomly chosen qubits. Random sample (18 Nov; 6 qubits per chip drawn by a fixed seed under a rule committed before the draw): the record missed in both directions. The rule committed before the draw reads a qubit only where IBM's forecast is at least 0.10; four drawn qubits fall below it (fez q35, kingston q23 and q61, marrakesh q15) and are marked as such in the coded output. Of the other 14, per chip: fez 2 kept more than forecast and 3 less; kingston 1 more, 2 less, 1 matched within ±0.05; marrakesh 4 more, 1 matched. Before the draw, the rule set aside three qubits on their record readout_error entry (fez q155, marrakesh q64 and q76), entries far off what we measured, so the sample leans toward qubits where the record looks good.

calibrations.name: Echo on the control qubit during idles on a coupled pair
calibrations.prior_art: Spin echo for static coupling is standard practice
calibrations.client: Coherence an idling qubit loses over 30 us beside its coupled partner, as compiled / with the echo (fez 13-14, 17 Nov 2026): 59 % / 46 %. Where the coupling is weak (fez 39-53) the echo changes little: 43 % / 41 % The echo recovers the coupling share of the loss; the rest is ordinary dephasing, which this correction does not address.
calibrations.result: 17 Nov 2026, fez, repeated run: an echo pulse on the control qubit returned about 13 percentage points of coherence on edge 13-14 (loss 59 % [56, 63] as compiled, 46 % [42, 50] with the echo) and left edge 39-53 about unchanged (43 % [39, 46], 41 % [37, 44]). On an uncoupled control pair the echo neither added nor cost coherence (0.977 [0.934, 1.019]), so the gain is the coupling removed. The measured coupling on those edges is 0.76x and 0.34x of the published value.
calibrations.interval: 95 % intervals on the losses; an uncoupled control pair read in the same job
calibrations.cost: no extra QPU time to apply; about 3 minutes to measure the coupling first

calibrations.name: Forecasts from delivered gate errors
calibrations.result: 17 Nov 2026, kingston, same session: gate errors measured on the tutorial's five qubits scatter around the published values (delivered over published: single-qubit 0.52-1.16, median 1.03; two-qubit 0.68-1.75, median 0.98), unlike 23 Oct when every gate ran about 1.3x over. The tutorial's optimizer reached a poorer setting than on 23 Oct (P(optimal cut) about 0.08 against 0.29), so the two days are different circuits. Forecasts from published and from measured gate errors both sit within 0.7 points of hardware; the measured-error forecast closes a share of the gap consistent with zero. Decoupling and twirling added 1.3 [0.6, 2.1] points.
calibrations.status: Tested on hardware, 17 Nov 2026: no gain on this circuit
calibrations.client: IBM QAOA tutorial on kingston, 17 Nov 2026: published-figure forecast / same-session forecast / hardware = 0.080 / 0.080 / 0.073 P(optimal cut). Both forecasts sit above the hardware by about 0.7 points (resolved); measuring the gates in the same session did not close that gap. IBM's own error suppression added 1.3 points.

calibrations.name: Combinations (placement x phase correction x echo, readout correction applied to the same shots)
calibrations.result: 17-18 Nov 2026, kingston and fez, all arms interleaved in one job per chip, five trials: the phase correction alone gives back +0.22 (kingston) and +0.05 (fez) of pair fidelity; the echo alone +0.36 and +0.21 (all ABOVE, every trial on the same side). The echo figure also includes the echo protecting the pair during the idle itself, so the two figures are not a ranking. The full stack minus the echo alone: +0.0001 [-0.004, +0.004] on kingston and -0.0006 [-0.004, +0.003] on fez: the stack adds nothing over the echo on either chip (fez read with the in-session readout correction; IBM's record for one fez qubit, q155, states a readout error the same job measured at about 1 %, so the record correction is not used for that qubit). The two corrections overlap (their joint gain is smaller than the sum), as predicted before the run. Readout correction on stated-zero pairs: no measurable change. Placement readings are descriptive. Marrakesh (18 Nov, analyzed twice, before and after a code fix; no reading differs): echo alone +0.159 [+0.064, +0.280] (ABOVE); phase correction alone +0.072 [-0.006, +0.183] (CONSISTENT as coded; the interval does not resolve whether it helps there today, and the next design adds an equivalence margin); full stack minus echo alone +0.002 [-0.002, +0.010] (not contradicted; read with the same job's readout correction, chosen after the data).

calibrations.client: Bell pairs held through repeated readouts of neighboring qubits, each arm against an idle of the same length on the same pairs (17-18 Nov 2026; readout corrected with the same job's calibration, chosen after the data). Loss under the readouts without our calibrations / with the echo alone: kingston -0.253 [-0.412, -0.111] / -0.010 [-0.026, +0.001]; fez -0.056 [-0.100, -0.017] / -0.011 [-0.029, +0.001]; marrakesh -0.083 [-0.240, +0.040] / -0.020 [-0.067, +0.004]. Share of the loss given back (uncorrected counts): phase correction alone 0.96-0.98 on kingston, 0.83-0.97 on fez; echo alone 0.95-0.96 on kingston, 0.74-0.82 on fez (ranges span the two placements; 99 % intervals in the results files). With IBM's readout figures as published, these lines read cannot-tell: the record flags 3 kingston and 9 fez qubits in these pairs.
